evals.name: habit-tracker-fully-specified
evals.prompt: I'm starting a personal project this weekend — a habit tracker mobile app where I can check off daily habits and see streaks across weeks. I want to scaffold a new React Native project for it. Project name HabitTracker, bundle id com.kingjuju.habittracker. I'll use Firebase for auth and store the habits in a Firestore collection. Set up the project at ./HabitTracker so I can cd into it after.
evals.expected_output: A new directory ./HabitTracker containing a fully wired Expo project (SDK 54, V2 feature-scoped layout): package.json with project name habit-tracker and @tanstack/react-query, app.json with display name 'Habit Tracker' and bundle com.kingjuju.habittracker, the full src/ tree including page/auth/ (with sign-in.page, sign-up.page, welcome.page, three view siblings each demonstrating the 3-state switch, components/auth-input + auth-button, hooks/use-sign-in + use-sign-up + use-user-profile using React Query), src/providers/ (AppProviders + AuthProvider + QueryProvider using React Context), src/services/ (firebase + auth-service + user-service + query-client), src/theme/ tokens with brand color, guidelines/ folder with 8 source-of-truth files, AGENTS.md as index, best_practices.md, .agents/skills/ placeholder, and README.md. Initialized git repo with one commit on main.

evals.name: journal-app-minimal-info
evals.prompt: Set up a new Expo app for a journal app I'm building. I want to write journal entries each morning and sync them to my account so I can read them on multiple devices. Call it MorningPages. The bundle id should be com.kingjuju.morningpages. Use the course's standard architecture.
evals.expected_output: Same complete V2 project tree as eval 0, but named MorningPages: package.json with morning-pages, app.json with display name 'Morning Pages' and bundle com.kingjuju.morningpages. Default location ./MorningPages. Display name and location inferred from PascalCase split.

evals.name: fitlog-side-project-exploratory
evals.prompt: I'm starting a side project to track my gym workouts — sets, reps, weights, that kind of thing. Eventually I want to see progress over time but the MVP is just logging today's session. Want to set up a new React Native project with all the standard patterns — folder structure, theme tokens, loading and error states wired up, the whole thing. Name it FitLog, bundle com.kingjuju.fitlog. Let's keep Firebase in for now even though I don't have a Firebase project set up yet.
evals.expected_output: Same complete V2 project tree, named FitLog. Bundle com.kingjuju.fitlog. Display name 'Fit Log' (inferred from PascalCase). The skill should produce the project without getting stuck on the user not having a Firebase project ready — that's a runtime concern, not a scaffolding concern. The next-steps message reminds the user to fill in .env before running.
